L0: # Search
L1: 
L2: Look up objects in your Stripe data.
L3: 
L4: Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)
L5: ## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins
L6: 
L7: Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.
L8: 
L9: **Quickstart**: Install the Stripe CLI with `npm install -g @stripe/cli` and run `stripe agent setup`.
L10: Some top level API resources support retrieval with search API methods. You can use the search APIs to retrieve your Stripe objects in a flexible manner. Using search is a faster alternative to [paginating](https://docs.stripe.com/api/pagination.md) through all resources. To create a search query, review the [Search query language](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#search-query-language) and reference the query fields of the resource:
L11: - [Query fields for Charges](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#query-fields-for-charges)
L12: - [Query fields for Customers](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#query-fields-for-customers)
L13: - [Query fields for Invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#query-fields-for-invoices)
L14: - [Query fields for PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#query-fields-for-paymentintents)
L15: - [Query fields for Prices](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#query-fields-for-prices)
L16: - [Query fields for Products](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#query-fields-for-products)
L17: - [Query fields for Subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#query-fields-for-subscriptions)
L18: ## Limitations
L19: ### Minimum API version
L20: 
L21: The minimum supported API Version to use search is `2020-08-27`. Read our [API upgrades guide](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md) to learn more about upgrades. To use search without upgrading your account API version, you can override the API version on a single request by setting the `Stripe-Version` request header:
L22: 
L23: ```bash
L24: -H "Stripe-Version: 2026-08-26.dahlia"
L25: ```
L26: Read our [SDKs](https://docs.stripe.com/sdks.md#versioning) guide on how to override an API version when using a library.
L27: ### Data freshness
L28: 
L29: Don’t use search for read-after-write flows (for example, searching immediately after a charge is made) because the data won’t be immediately available to search. Under normal operating conditions, data is searchable in under 1 minute. Propagation of new or updated data could be delayed during an outage.
L30: For read-after-write flows that require immediate data availability, use the various list APIs, such as [List invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/list.md)). These APIs aren’t subject to the availability delays mentioned above.
L31: ### Data mismatches
L32: 
L33: In some cases, the data you use to find search results might not match the results that you receive. This can happen because the Search API filters using a cached version of the PaymentIntent `status`, but returns data based on the latest version of the PaymentIntent.
L34: For example, if you query the [Search Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/search.md) for PaymentIntents with the status `requires_capture`, it might return some PaymentIntents with the status `succeeded`. This happens because the Search API finds cached PaymentIntents that have the older `requires_capture` status, but returns the current `succeeded` status in the results.
L35: ### Rate limits
L36: We apply a [rate limit](https://docs.stripe.com/rate-limits.md) of up to 20 read operations per second which applies for all search endpoints in live mode and test environments. Live mode and test environment limits are separate. Keeping the rate limit in mind, for workloads where you need to run analytics on one or more API resources, [Sigma](https://docs.stripe.com/data/how-sigma-works.md) is much more efficient.
L37: For workloads where you need to export a large portion of your API resource, our [Data Pipeline](https://docs.stripe.com/data/access-data-in-warehouse.md) product is more efficient.
L38: ### Regional availability
L39: 
L40: Search isn’t available to businesses in India.
L41: ### Test clock objects omitted in list all results
L42: 
L43: Stripe list APIs (such as [List invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/list.md)) omit results generated by test clocks for list all requests. To see results generated by test clocks in these cases, you must request results within a specific parent, such as `test_clock`, `customer`, or `subscription`.
L44: For example, `GET /v1/invoices` won’t return test clock generated invoices, but `GET /v1/invoices/{customer_id}` returns all invoices for that customer, including those that are test clock generated.
L45: 
L46: Similarly, you can specify a test clock ID in this example to get all invoices related to that test clock, or you can specify a subscription ID to return all invoices billed for that subscription, including test clock generated invoices.
L47: ### Pagination
L48: 
L49: In rare cases, paginating through a result set can reorder some records, causing them to be missing or duplicated on a page. If you encounter this issue, contact us using the form at [Stripe support](https://support.stripe.com).
L50: 
L51: ## Examples
L52: 
L53: Here are some examples of what you can do with the [Search charges API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/search.md) and [Search Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/search.md):
L54: ### Charges metadata search
L55: 
L56: Look up charges matching a custom metadata value.
L57: 
L58: ```curl
L59: curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/search \
L60:   -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
L61:   --data-urlencode "query=metadata['key']:'value'"
L62: ```
L63: 
L64: ### Charges last4 search
L65: 
L66: Look up charges matching the last 4 digits of the card used for the payment.
L67: 
L68: ```curl
L69: curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/search \
L70:   -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
L71:   --data-urlencode "query=payment_method_details.card.last4:4242"
L72: ```
L73: ### Customers email search
L74: 
L75: Look up customers matching an email.
L76: 
L77: ```curl
L78: curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/search \
L79:   -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
L80:   --data-urlencode "query=email:'sally@rocketrides.io'"
L81: ```
L82: 
L83: ### Negation filter
L84: 
L85: Look up PaymentIntents not in the USD currency.
L86: 
L87: ```curl
L88: curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/payment_intents/search \
L89:   -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
L90:   --data-urlencode "query=-currency:'usd'"
L91: ```
L92: ### Numeric filter
L93: 
L94: Filter invoice objects with a `total` greater than 1000.
L95: 
L96: ```curl
L97: curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/invoices/search \
L98:   -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
L99:   -d "query=total>1000"
L100: ```
L101: 
L102: ### Combining multiple filters
L103: 
L104: Look up charges matching a combination of metadata and currency.
L105: 
L106: ```curl
L107: curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges/search \
L108:   -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>:" \
L109:   --data-urlencode "query=metadata['key']:'value' AND currency:'usd'"
L110: ```
L111: 
L112: ## Search query language
L113: ### Query structure and terminology
L114: 
L115: A query `clause` consists of a `field` followed by an `operator` followed by a `value`:
L116: 
L117: |  |
L118: | clause | `email:"amy@rocketrides.io"` |
L119: | field | `email` |
L120: | operator | `:` |
L121: | value | `amy@rocketrides.io` |
L122: You can combine up to 10 query clauses in a search by either separating them with a space, or using the `AND` or `OR` keywords (case insensitive). You can’t combine `AND` and `OR` in the same query. Furthermore, there’s no option to use parentheses to give priority to certain logic operators. By default, the API combines clauses with `AND` logic.
L123: The example query `email:"amy@rocketrides.io" metadata["key"]:"value"` matches records where both the email address is amy@rocketrides.io, and the metadata in the record includes `key` with a value of `value`.
L124: ### Creating a query which doesn’t match a clause
L125: 
L126: You can negate query clauses using a `-` character. For example, the following search returns records that don’t match the email `amy@rocketrides.io`.
L127: 
L128: `-email:"amy@rocketrides.io"`
L129: ### Field types, substring matching, and numeric comparators
L130: 
L131: Every search field supports exact matching with a `:`. Certain fields such as `email` and `name` support substring matching. Certain other fields such as `amount` support numeric comparators like `>` and `<`.
L132: Each field includes a type that defines the operations you can use in the field. For a full list of available fields, see [supported query fields for each resource](https://docs.stripe.com/search.md#supported-query-fields-for-each-resource).
L133: 
L134: Using an unsupported operator, such as specifying greater than (`>`) on a string, returns an error.
L135: 
L136: | type | operators |
L137: | --- | --- |
L138: | token | exact match (case insensitive) |
L139: | string | exact match, substring (case insensitive)
L140: An exact match on a string type returns any record where that record contains all of the words from the query in the same order. For example the query `name:"one two three"` would match both a result with the name “one two three” and a result with the name “one two three four”. |
L141: | numeric | exact match, greater than and less than |
L142: ### Quotes
L143: 
L144: You must use quotation marks around string values. Quotation marks are optional for numeric values. For example:
L145: 
L146: - `currency:"usd"` means quotes are required.
L147: - `payment_method_details.card.last4:1234` means quotes are optional.
L148: 
L149: You can escape quotes inside of quotes with a backslash (`\`).
L150: 
L151: `description:"the story called \"The Sky and the Sea.\""`
L152: ### Metadata
L153: 
L154: You can perform searches on [metadata](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata.md) that you’ve added to objects that support it.
L155: 
L156: Use the following format to construct a clause for a metadata search: `metadata["<field>"]:"<value>"`.
L157: 
L158: The following clause demonstrates how to create a clause that queries for records with a donation ID of “asdf-jkl”: `metadata["donation-id"]:"asdf-jkl"`.
L159: You can query for the presence of a metadata key on an object. The following clause would match all records where `donation-id` is a metadata key. `-metadata["donation-id"]:null`
L160: ### Search Syntax
L161: 
L162: The following table lists the syntax that you can use to construct a query.
L163: | Syntax | Usage | Description | Examples |
L164: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
L165: | `:` | `field:value` | Exact match operator (case insensitive) | `currency:"eur"` returns records where the currency is exactly “EUR” in a case-insensitive comparison |
L166: | `AND`, `and` | `field:value1 AND field:value2` | The query returns only records that match both clauses (case insensitive) | `status:"active" AND amount:500` |
L167: | `OR`, `or` | `field:value1 OR field:value2` | The query returns records that match either of the clauses (case insensitive) | `currency:"usd" OR currency:"eur"` |
L168: | `-` | `-field:value` | Returns records that don’t match the clause | `-currency:"jpy"` returns records that aren’t in JPY |
L169: | `NULL`, `null` | `field:null` | A special token used for field presence (case insensitive) | `url:null` returns records where a URL field is empty |
L170: | `\` | `" \"\""` | Escape quotes within quotes | `description:"the story called \"The Sky and the Sea.\""` |
L171: | `~` | `field~value` | Substring match operator (substrings must be a minimum of 3 characters) | `email~"amy"` returns matches for amy@rocketrides.io and xamy |
L172: | `>`, `<`, `=` | - `field<value`
L173: - `field>value`
L174: - `field>=value`
L175: - `field<=value` | Greater than/less than operators | `amount>="10"` brings up objects where the amount is 10 or greater |
L176: ## Supported query fields for each resource
L177: ### Query fields for Charges
L178: | Field | usage | Type (token, string, numeric) |
L179: | --- | --- | --- |
L180: | amount | `amount>1000` | numeric |
L181: | billing_details.address.postal_code | `billing_details.address.postal_code:12345` | token |
L182: | created | `created>1620310503` | numeric |
L183: | currency | `currency:"usd"` | token |
L184: | customer | `customer:"cus_123"` | token |
L185: | disputed | `disputed:"true"` | token |
L186: | metadata | `metadata["key"]:"value"` | token |
L187: | payment_method_details.{{SOURCE}}.last4 | `payment_method_details.card.last4:1234` | token |
L188: | payment_method_details.{{SOURCE}}.exp_month | `payment_method_details.card_present.exp_month:12` | token |
L189: | payment_method_details.{{SOURCE}}.exp_year | `payment_method_details.interac_present.exp_year:2022` | token |
L190: | payment_method_details.{{SOURCE}}.brand | `payment_method_details.card.brand:"visa"` | token |
L191: | payment_method_details.{{SOURCE}}.fingerprint | `payment_method_details.card.fingerprint:"fp"` | token |
L192: | payment_method_details.{{SOURCE}}.reader | `payment_method_details.card_present.reader:"tmr_FDOt2wlRZEdpd7"` | token |
L193: | payment_method_details.{{SOURCE}}.location | `payment_method_details.interac_present.location:"tml_FBakXQG8bQk4Mm"` | token |
L194: | refunded | `refunded:"true"` | token |
L195: | status | `status:"succeeded"` | token |
L196: For `SOURCE`, use `card`, `card_present`, `interac_present`, or any of the [additional payment methods that Terminal supports](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/payments/additional-payment-methods.md). Use `card` for online charges, `interac_present` for Terminal card present charges for the Interac network, and `card_present` for other Terminal card present charges.
L197: When querying for Terminal-related fields not specific to cards, such as `reader` and `location`, you can also use other payment methods such as `wechat_pay`.
L198: 
L199: The `disputed` field accepts only the tokens “true” and “false”, indicating the presence of disputes.
L200: 
L201: `refunded:"true"` filters for fully-refunded charges, `refunded:"false"` filters for charges that haven’t been refunded at all or have been partially refunded, and `refunded:null` filters for non-refunded charges.
